criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission concept, users, and rationale with references. Lacks formal requirements but strong overall.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Plan presented with Gantt and task descriptions, but no explicit contingencies or variation provisions; feasible.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Minor work completed; no technical results or simulations yet; insufficient interpretation.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure and readable, but reference list mismatch and figure not properly labelled; formatting mostly consistent.

technical_issues.issue: Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic is technically inaccurate; ocean acidification is a pH decrease, not a 30% increase in acidity.
Gantt chart lacks a figure caption/number.
Reference list includes sources not cited in text; in-text footnotes are separate, so reference list does not match citations.
No explicit mission requirements (e.g., orbit, resolution, revisit time) are stated.
No contingency provisions or variation plans in the project plan.

overall: Good mission concept and rationale with references, but preliminary technical progress is minimal and project plan lacks contingencies. Presentation is readable but reference list mismatch and missing figure caption. Overall a solid preliminary report.

feedback.summary: Your preliminary report presents a clear, well-referenced mission concept for coral reef monitoring, with a feasible project plan and readable structure. To strengthen it, add formal mission requirements, include contingency provisions in your plan, present preliminary technical results beyond tutorials, and align your reference list with in-text citations. Also add a caption for your Gantt chart and correct the ocean acidification statement.
next_steps: Add explicit mission requirements (orbit, resolution, revisit time) and correct the ocean acidification claim in Mission Concept & Rationale.
Extend your Project Plan with contingency/variation provisions and explain how the plan links to the mission concept; include references to information sources.
Include preliminary technical results (e.g., STK orbit/coverage analysis) with brief interpretation, and fix presentation: caption the Gantt chart and ensure reference list matches in-text citations.

criteria.C1: You clearly describe the mission to monitor the Great Barrier Reef, identify users (marine and conservation scientists), and support the rationale with references. To strengthen within Accomplished, add explicit mission requirements (orbit, resolution, revisit time) and correct the ocean acidification statement—acidification is a pH decrease, not a 30% increase in acidity.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task descriptions show a feasible plan, but it lacks contingency provisions and variation plans. To reach Accomplished, add contingencies, explain why the plan is structured this way in the context of your mission concept, and include references to your information sources.
criteria.C3: You have completed STK tutorials 1–4, but preliminary technical progress is minimal. To reach Accomplished, include a good preliminary set of results (e.g., orbit trade study, coverage or link budget) with brief description and interpretation, and show you are clearly on track for completion.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear structure and is readable, but the reference list includes sources not cited in text and your Gantt chart (Image 1) lacks a figure caption/number. To reach Accomplished, ensure every reference list entry is cited in text and vice versa, add captions/numbers to figures, and maintain consistent formatting throughout.
